events.description: A sustained plume of dust and debris rises from the left side of a building on a hillside, expanding and drifting rightward over ~19 seconds without visible fire or secondary blasts.

verification.reason: The continuous, voluminous dust cloud originating from a localized point (left wall/adjacent structure) with rapid initial expansion and gradual dissipation is consistent with a single explosive event (e.g., demolition or blast), not ongoing fire, collapse, or natural landslide; all three candidates overlap this same visible phenomenon and are merged into one event.

events.description: A sudden violent blast at t=34.5 (f3) ejects debris and a bright flash, followed by rapidly expanding dust cloud engulfing the building through f22 (47.5).

verification.reason: Frame f3 shows an abrupt onset of a bright flash and outward ejection of material consistent with a high-energy blast; subsequent frames (f4–f22) show progressive expansion and settling of a massive dust/debris cloud originating from the structure—diagnostic of an explosion, not collapse or fire alone.

events.description: A building is rapidly enveloped and obscured by a large, expanding cloud of dust and debris, consistent with a structural collapse triggered by an explosion.

verification.reason: The sudden onset of dense, turbulent dust at f4 (50.0 s), rapid expansion and obscuration of the building through f12–f19, and absence of fire or sustained combustion indicate a blast-induced collapse rather than fire or demolition-by-removal; the dust plume dynamics match explosive disintegration.
